title: watchOS denies BSD sockets to third-party apps (EHOSTUNREACH on every dial — LAN, public v4, public v6 — on both the BT proxy and the watch's own wifi; proven on the Series 10 2026-08-23 via the caps.scala http error line), so Go's net stack can never dial from the wrist and every simulator net gate passed only because the simulator shares the host's stack. Fix: an HttpDo over NSURLSession — purego, DELEGATE-based (didReceiveData/didCompleteWithError; no Obj-C blocks), the same shape as macaudio's delegates — behind the caps.scala capability seam that exists for exactly this; it also rides the Bluetooth phone proxy, which raw sockets never would. iroh/QUIC (UDP) sits behind the same wall — separate question, note in sgola-ffi/wata-watch docs. Until this lands the watch client cannot log in on hardware and WATCH-AUDIO's receive half is blocked

title: plan 0069 stage 3 REMAINDER. Done 2026-08-19: go-pkgs/macaudio runs on watchOS unmodified - engine, playback, real microphone capture and both codec ends (just watch-spike --only audio), and both audio modules cross-build for the device sysroot including the cgo one. wata-watch links the audio thread and watch-e2e runs it with macaudio's fake ends. What is LEFT is the round trip on real hardware: hold-to-talk recording through the long-press edges, and playback of a received message, neither of which has happened with real audio on a wrist. The mic permission alert on first press is expected, not a bug (see the plan). HARDWARE FINDINGS 2026-08-23 (first wrist session): the record half WORKS — real long-press edges drove real mic capture twice ('capture input 48000 Hz, 1 ch', 'audio: recorded ms=640 ogg=2202') — but (1) RESOLVED: a counted 3s hold recorded ms=3720 — duration tracks the hold, the 640s were just short holds; capture drain is healthy. (2) the THIRD rapid hold crashed the app mid-capture: SIGSEGV KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x10 in objc_msgSend, called from purego syscallX on the audio thread — a dead objc object during capture teardown/restart, the watch cousin of the iOS rapid-episode '!con'. Crash report WataWatch-2026-08-23-105312.ips; REPRODUCED ON DEMAND same day: a ~3s hold, then a quick second hold — dies right after the second capture-start line, every time so far. Playback half stays blocked on WATCH-URLSESSION-HTTP (no session without networking)
